chapter: Return to Chicago: the Blue Note and Rupneck's
title: Freddie Williamson's offer to lead the Dixielanders at the Blue Note
summary: Williamson offers $225 for Hodes and $175 for the men to bring a band to the Blue Note. Hodes assembles Pee Wee, Freddie Moore, Chippy Hill, Floyd O'Brien and Lee Collins.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: And just about the end of December, Freddie Williamson again calls me.
He's in Chicago, and now he's Glaser's man, second in command. Would you want to come to Chicago, to the Blue Note? With the Dixielanders? We want to do something here.

And you get the band, but don't tell me the plan. He just tells me to get the band. Offers me $225 for myself and $175 for the men. I haven't seen $225 since I've been in New York. Even in accumulation, I haven't seen it. I'm driving a car that my wife sold before I left New York for five dollars. A Ford, that same Ford.
The cops are stopping me and saying to me, you look sad behind the wheel. I have to curb it to stop it because --

1949 is when we left. '50, I left. I have to curb it, I don't have brakes, I can't afford them. We're not -- just ain't doing it, man, I don't know. My father put up the money for the house or we wouldn't have had a house. Money was something I had no quarrel with, I just didn't have any.
So here $225 is offered me. And the front all-star
group. Fine, I'm going to take Pee Wee Russell, I got Freddie Moore, he'll come, I'll take Chippy Hill, how many more? That's enough, we'll pick the rest of them in Chicago.

Fine, get to Chicago, okay, give you -- you can have Floyd O'Brien, if you want him. Okay, I want Floyd. Trumpet, give you Lee Collins. Fine, we can't afford no bass, that's it. And we're playing, and it's tremendous. Because we're working opposite either Errol Garner, Sarah Vaughan, we're working opposite those kind of people so the joint is packed.
